next_row.boundary_rationale: This row opens on Babylon's own gods collapsing: “Bel bows down. Nebo stoops. Their idols are carried by animals, and on the livestock. The things that you carried around are heavy loads, a burden for the weary.” (web:Isa.46.1) sets the idols of Bel and Nebo onto pack animals as dead weight, their load named with the ordinary carrying-noun מַשָּׂ֖א לַעֲיֵפָֽה (oshb:Isa.46.1, byte tier) -- a burden common noun in this idol-procession scene, not a verse-initial oracle header of the massa series. The same noun recurs as the idols themselves cannot rescue what they carry: “They stoop and they bow down together. They could not deliver the burden, but they have gone into captivity.” (web:Isa.46.2), spliced at מַלֵּ֣ט מַשָּׂ֑א (oshb:Isa.46.2, byte tier) -- the burden noun here matching Isa.46.1's at accent-stripped tier only, not byte (tipcha there against etnachta here) -- closing the tableau on their own captivity. Two root-level devices bridge into the following verses that an English gloss alone would leave undisclosed: the load-bearer participles נְשֻׂאֹתֵיכֶ֣ם עֲמוּס֔וֹת (oshb:Isa.46.1) answered by הַֽעֲמֻסִים֙ מִנִּי בֶ֔טֶן הַנְּשֻׂאִ֖ים מִנִּי רָֽחַם (oshb:Isa.46.3) -- disjoint under consonantal search, the plene and defective spellings each standing in exactly 1 verse at skeleton tier, so the tie is root-level and not a form recurrence -- and the rescue root at Isa.46.2 answered by וַאֲמַלֵּֽט (oshb:Isa.46.4), skeleton tier (sweep: 7 verses book-wide). Neither device is treated as reason enough to hold this tableau and the following address in one unit, since web:Isa.46.3 turns the discourse from third-person description to a first-person vocative with a named addressee, the stronger seam signal here.

They could not deliver the burden, but they have gone into captivity.” (web:Isa.46.2), spliced at מַלֵּ֣ט מַשָּׂ֑א (oshb:Isa.46.2, byte tier) -- the burden noun here matching Isa.46.1's at accent-stripped tier only, not byte (tipcha there against etnachta here) -- closing the tableau on their own captivity. prev_row.boundary_rationale: A rhetorical question opens this span at web:Isa.49.24, “Shall the plunder be taken from the mighty, or the lawful captives be delivered?”, rendered pointed as הֲיֻקַּ֥ח מִגִּבּ֖וֹר מַלְק֑וֹחַ וְאִם שְׁבִ֥י צַדִּ֖יק יִמָּלֵֽט (oshb:Isa.49.24, tier: byte), distinct in form from the preceding promise addressed to the nations. An answering 'for thus says Yahweh' formula follows at web:Isa.49.25, pointed כִּי כֹ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה גַּם שְׁבִ֤י גִבּוֹר֙ יֻקָּ֔ח וּמַלְק֥וֹחַ עָרִ֖יץ יִמָּלֵ֑ט וְאֶת יְרִיבֵךְ֙ אָנֹכִ֣י אָרִ֔יב וְאֶת בָּנַ֖יִךְ אָנֹכִ֥י אוֹשִֽׁיעַ (oshb:Isa.49.25, tier: byte) — its own leading causal particle, כִּי, marks this inventoried divine frame as the answer to the question just posed rather than a fresh onset dividing the span — and the span closes at web:Isa.49.26, “I will feed those who oppress you with their own flesh; and they will be drunk on their own blood, as with sweet wine. Then all flesh shall know that I, Yahweh, am your Savior and your Redeemer, the Mighty One of Jacob.””, in pointed form וְהַאֲכַלְתִּ֤י אֶת מוֹנַ֨יִךְ֙ אֶת בְּשָׂרָ֔ם וְכֶעָסִ֖יס דָּמָ֣ם יִשְׁכָּר֑וּן וְיָדְע֣וּ כָל בָּשָׂ֗ר כִּ֣י אֲנִ֤י יְהוָה֙ מֽוֹשִׁיעֵ֔ךְ וְגֹאֲלֵ֖ךְ אֲבִ֥יר יַעֲקֹֽב (oshb:Isa.49.26, tier: byte), on the self-identification formula “I, Yahweh, am your Savior and your Redeemer.” At oshb:Isa.49.23, just before this span opens, a parashah SAMEKH mark (single-witness) brings the preceding material to a close. A further parashah SAMEKH mark is found where this span itself ends, at oshb:Isa.49.26, witnessed in a single source.

next_row.boundary_rationale: A first-person voice distinct from the preceding divine self-vindication opens this span at web:Isa.50.4, “The Lord Yahweh has given me the tongue of those who are taught, that I may know how to sustain with words him who is weary. He awakens morning by morning, he awakens my ear to hear as those who are taught.”, pointed אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהֹוִ֗ה נָ֤תַן לִי֙ לְשׁ֣וֹן לִמּוּדִ֔ים לָדַ֛עַת לָע֥וּת אֶת יָעֵ֖ף דָּבָ֑ר יָעִ֣יר בַּבֹּ֣קֶר בַּבֹּ֗קֶר יָעִ֥יר לִי֙ אֹ֔זֶן לִשְׁמֹ֖עַ כַּלִּמּוּדִֽים (oshb:Isa.50.4, tier: byte), describing an ear wakened morning by morning to hear. The same first-person voice reports its obedience under attack at web:Isa.50.5-Isa.50.6, pointed אֲדֹנָ֤י יְהוִה֙ פָּתַֽח לִ֣י אֹ֔זֶן וְאָנֹכִ֖י לֹ֣א מָרִ֑יתִי אָח֖וֹר לֹ֥א נְסוּגֹֽתִי (oshb:Isa.50.5, tier: byte), and its confidence that “the Lord Yahweh will help me” through web:Isa.50.7-Isa.50.9, pointed הֵ֣ן אֲדֹנָ֤י יְהוִה֙ יַֽעֲזָר לִ֔י מִי ה֖וּא יַרְשִׁיעֵ֑נִי הֵ֤ן כֻּלָּם֙ כַּבֶּ֣גֶד יִבְל֔וּ עָ֖שׁ יֹאכְלֵֽם (oshb:Isa.50.9, tier: byte). A rhetorical-wisdom address then turns to a wider audience at web:Isa.50.10, “Who among you fears Yahweh and obeys the voice of his servant?” pointed מִ֤י בָכֶם֙ יְרֵ֣א יְהוָ֔ה שֹׁמֵ֖עַ בְּק֣וֹל עַבְדּ֑וֹ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָלַ֣ךְ חֲשֵׁכִ֗ים וְאֵ֥ין נֹ֨גַהּ֙ ל֔וֹ יִבְטַח֙ בְּשֵׁ֣ם יְהוָ֔ה וְיִשָּׁעֵ֖ן בֵּאלֹהָֽיו (oshb:Isa.50.10, tier: byte), and the span closes with a warning to a different addressee at web:Isa.50.11, “Behold, all you who kindle a fire, who adorn yourselves with torches around yourselves, walk in the flame of your fire, and among the torches that you have kindled. You will have this from my hand: you will lie down in sorrow.”, in pointed form הֵ֧ן כֻּלְּכֶ֛ם קֹ֥דְחֵי אֵ֖שׁ מְאַזְּרֵ֣י זִיק֑וֹת לְכ֣וּ בְּא֣וּר אֶשְׁכֶ֗ם וּבְזִיקוֹת֙ בִּֽעַרְתֶּ֔ם מִיָּדִי֙ הָיְתָה זֹּ֣את לָכֶ֔ם לְמַעֲצֵבָ֖ה תִּשְׁכָּבֽוּן (oshb:Isa.50.11, tier: byte). This row holds web:Isa.50.10-Isa.50.11 attached to the first-person report as one span because no massa, hoy, or fresh messenger-formula frame opens the turn at web:Isa.50.10 -- it is a wisdom-style rhetorical question that still names “his servant” as its topic. The turn does carry the same addressee-shift signal this cluster treats as tier-1 elsewhere (the imperative summonses opening web:Isa.51.1, web:Isa.51.4 and web:Isa.51.7 are driven on that class alone): web:Isa.50.10 opens with a fresh second-person-plural interrogative, מִ֤י בָכֶם֙ (oshb:Isa.50.10, tier: byte), addressed to a plural audience rather than continuing the servant's own first-person voice. This row applies that same category here and still holds the attachment, on the ground that no frame token accompanies the shift and the topic itself, “his servant,” does not change. Immediately before this span's onset, a parashah SAMEKH mark (single-witness) sits at oshb:Isa.50.3; a further PE mark (single-witness) sits at this span's own close, oshb:Isa.50.11; the parashah paragraph itself carries no internal break at oshb:Isa.50.10, disclosed here as tier-3 single-witness corroboration only, never the ground for the hold. Paseq marks (single-witness, count-only) sit at oshb:Isa.50.4, oshb:Isa.50.10 and oshb:Isa.50.11, three sites inside this span.
